text:
maria: Heads-up — I pushed a terraform change to upgrade gpu-pool-us-west2 from nv4b -> nv6 to avoid OOMs on dedicated jobs. The GitOps pre-merge ran Conftest/OPA and blocked because we’re inside the freeze window. Need either an exemption or a quick plan to avoid customer impact.

sam: Can you paste the Conftest/OPA output? quick glance helps.

maria: Here’s the relevant snippet from the CI logs: 
```
FAIL - policy: freeze-window
resource: google_compute_instance_group.gpu-pool-us-west2
message: change disallowed during freeze window (2026-04-10T00:00Z -> 2026-04-12T23:59Z)
rule: deny_if_during_freeze
file: modules/gpu-pools/main.tf:42
```

jin: Ok. So the policy is doing what it should. Is this an emergency capacity issue or a regular scheduled upgrade?

maria: Emergency — we started seeing retries and OOMs on heavy training jobs this morning. If we don’t add capacity overnight some dedicated customers will hit hard failure rates by tomorrow. Metrics: https://playback.internal/redwood/metrics/gpu-pool-us-west2 (link).

kai: Two quick options: 1) wait until freeze window ends and schedule the upgrade (low risk) or 2) request an emergency exemption and do a canary-first rollout. Which do we prefer?

maria: We need option 2 unless we want to take support tickets. I’ll file an exemption request — @ops-approvals-bot can you start the approval flow? Reason: emergency capacity to prevent customer OOMs, PR: gitlab.com/redwood/infra/merge_requests/789

ops-approvals-bot: Exemption request submitted. id=APP-1234. Status=awaiting-approver(eng-infra-leads). Please include rollback plan and canary strategy in the request metadata.

sam: I’ll take approval duty for this one. Conditions: 1) limit to a canary pool of 2 nv6 instances, 2) disable autoscale for the canary group during the rollout, 3) add explicit rollback tfvars and test a plan against a staging cluster first. If you add those to the MR I’ll approve.

maria: Copy — adding canary.tfvars and the plan steps now. Plan command I’m going to run: `TF_LOG=info terraform plan -var-file=canary.tfvars -target=module.gpu_pool_us_west2` and then apply against the canary branch.

jin: +1 from me once the staging plan is green and logs show no eviction spikes. Also please add a short postmortem ticket template in case canary fails so we can revert quickly.

kai: FYI ops: if we approve, make sure Conftest still runs but skips freeze-window rule for APP-1234 id only — we should avoid adding permanent ignores.

ops-approvals-bot: APP-1234 updated with canary strategy and rollback fields. Notifying approvers: sam, jin.

sam: Approved APP-1234 (manual override for emergency capacity). Comments: keep canary <=2, monitor for 2h, automatic rollback if error_rate > 3x baseline.

jin: Acked.

maria: Thanks all. I’m going to push the canary branch now, run the staging plan, and then apply once staging looks healthy. I’ll post the apply logs and the APP-1234 approval link in the MR.

deploy-bot: gitops-check: canary branch plan success — no other policy failures after exemption applied to APP-1234.

maria: Closing loop here — canary applied, monitoring for 2h. Will open a short incident ticket if anything regresses and will revert to nv4b if we see >3x errors.

kai: Nice work. Suggest we follow up with a brief doc on emergency exemption criteria so approvals are faster next time.

maria: Agreed — adding to eng-infra runbook.
